newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli defence minister sees Egyptian president.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence minister sees Egyptian president.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Hurghada on Tuesday in an attempt to save relations between Israel and Egypt.
They will also discuss the latest developments in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on the West Bank town of Hebron, which seemed on Tuesday to be moving closer to an agreement, officials said.
It is Mordechai's first visit to Egypt since he and his rightwing Likud party were elected in May.
Egypt, the first Arab state to make peace with Israel, has been a vociferous critic of Likud policies, especially its drive to expand settlements in the West Bank.
Visits to Egypt by Israeli ministers have become much less frequent than under the previous Labour Party government.
On Monday Mordechai said: "I hope that in this meeting we will succeed in strengthening relations between the two countries and to find ways to cooperate to advance the peace."
"Egypt plays an important role in the advancement of the peace process since it was the first Arab state to sign a peace agreement with Israel," he added in a statement.
